title: Broad Lean Corpus Build and Rich Isomorphism Status v0

canonical_node.axiom: The broader Lean corpus contains a richer structural testing layer that goes beyond equation-shape analogy, and this layer is verified by a successful full build with no active proof escapes.
definitions: Rich isomorphism: a mapping that preserves roles, transitions, signature discipline, gate behavior, and passes adversarial wrong-swap checks.
Proof escape: active use of sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in source files (excluding expected #check_failure diagnostics).
Seed kernel: the minimal no-sorry package with 4 front-loaded assumptions and 17 starter theorems.
Broad corpus: the larger Lean archive with rich isomorphism/signature/adversarial layers and reported 287 theorems.
derivation: A full `lake build` completed successfully with 17 jobs.
A regex scan for sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe found no active proof escapes in main source files.
Targeted builds for Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, and other modules all passed.
The corpus docs list RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, no_rich_iso_to_natural_coin, richRelabeledCoinIso, BridgeMatrix, MasterEquationInvariance, and wrong-swap rejection rows.
The richer layer tests role preservation, transition preservation, signature discipline, gate behavior, and adversarial wrong-swap failures.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the broad corpus as a separate build layer from the seed kernel; do not merge until theorem inventory is normalized and wrapper/trivial rows are separated from substantive rows.
boundary: Lean verifies the encoded structure, not the domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Physics, theology, history, and source-grounding still carry the burden of domain fidelity.
The reported 287 theorems are from corpus docs and not independently verified in this document.
test: Run the proof-escape scan and confirm no active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe in main source files.
Check that the rich isomorphism layer includes the listed components and that wrong-swap checks fail for false mappings.

dg1_dependencies: Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, and other module sources
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a richer structural testing layer that rejects weak equation-shape analogies and enforces signature discipline and adversarial checks.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the seed kernel's clean compressed assumption spine and its no-sorry starter theorems.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without the rich isomorphism layer, the framework would rely merely on equation-shape analogy, losing the ability to distinguish intended mappings from false ones.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Record as a verified build status and rich isomorphism layer claim; do not treat as proof of domain fidelity.

overstatement_risks: Claiming Lean proves domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Treating the reported 287 theorems as independently verified.
Assuming the rich isomorphism layer is fully sound without inspecting the actual Lean code.
kill_conditions: If a full build fails on a clean checkout.
If active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe are found in main source files.
If the rich isomorphism layer is shown to be absent or non-functional.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the rich isomorphism layer in Lean and verify that intended mappings pass while false mappings fail.

plain_summary: This document reports that a broad Lean corpus builds successfully with no active proof escapes and includes a richer isomorphism layer that goes beyond equation-shape analogy. It emphasizes that Lean verifies the encoded structure, not the domain-faithfulness of human labels, and recommends keeping the broad corpus separate from the seed kernel until the theorem inventory is normalized.
